validity_note: Premise holds. Corrections: sessions are not stored in Redis (stateless HMAC-signed JWT cookies; OAuth registration sessions are an in-memory map in every mode), yet every authenticated request depends on the Redis user cache; only the rate limiter has a runtime fallback; no-redis is a startup-time storage.mode switch that lacks in-memory counterparts for step-up and email verification.

key_facts.claim: storage.mode (default redis) picks RedisUserCache|InMemoryUserCache, RedisRateLimiterService|InMemoryRateLimiterService, RedisGeoLocationCache|InMemoryGeoLocationCache, StorageRateLimitService|InMemoryStorageRateLimitService via @ConditionalOnProperty; GdprCompliantRateLimiterService fixes its delegate in the constructor. no-redis also sets spring.data.redis.enabled=false, excludes RedisAutoConfiguration, uses the simple cache and disables redis health.

RedisUserCache getters run GET outside try/catch (only cacheUser catches); the DB is consulted only on a miss. JwtAuthenticationFilter calls isUserActive/getTokenVersion inside a try whose catch returns 401 invalid_token for private endpoints and continues anonymously for public ones.

No recovery path: /auth/refresh-session is non-public (also 401); login maps the error to 401 token_exchange_failed; the FE treats a 401 refresh as a hard failure, clears the session and redirects to sign-in.

Rate limiting degrades: Lua calls run through a Resilience4j circuit breaker that falls back to per-instance in-memory windows (prod: threshold 3, open 10s, fallback-to-memory true); rate-limit.redis.enable-fallback is read by no code.

Geo-IP degrades: cache get/put catch and return null, so lookups go to MaxMind; tryLock/releaseLock do not catch (weekly DB-update job throws). If Redis calls hang past the 500 ms travel-check timeout, checks fail open, but after 5 consecutive failures fail closed for ADMIN/PENDING_ADMIN/COMPANY sessions whose IP changed.

Redis-only features fail hard: StepUpAuthService (codes, attempts, cooldown, lockout, tokens) and EmailVerificationService (oobCode->uid|email) have no fallback; signed-URL uploads call checkUploadAllowed/hasStorageSpace, which fail open only when the RedisTemplate is null (the fail-open checkAndRecordUpload has no caller); @Cacheable citiesCache has no CacheErrorHandler.

Evictions inside transactions roll back writes: evict has no try/catch, and archiveUser and re-consent evict inside @Transactional; admin cascade evicts after Firebase/Firestore/Storage are already deleted.

Health: prod enables Boot's redis indicator and UploadSystemHealthIndicator probes Redis, so overall /actuator/health goes DOWN; readiness (db,diskSpace,liquibase) and liveness (ping) stay UP; the prod compose healthcheck uses overall health. NoOpRedisHealthIndicator reports UP when storage.mode=in-memory.

Unaffected: cookie sessions are HMAC/JWT-validated with no server store, SocialAuthSessionService is an in-memory map, ShedLock uses JDBC, public endpoints continue anonymously. Prod Redis is one master plus one sentinel (no replica), allkeys-lru.

gaps.finding: Static wiring shows no-redis cannot start: StepUpAuthService and EmailVerificationService require StringRedisTemplate unconditionally, but no-redis excludes RedisAutoConfiguration and disables RedisConfiguration. This contradicts CONTRIBUTING.md's 'swaps every Redis-backed component'.

A Redis outage becomes a full authenticated outage reported as 401 (not 503) and an FE mass logout, although Postgres (source of truth) is up and the cache holds five fields; there is no DB fallback or breaker on errors and no Redis exception handler.

Startup validation does not enforce anything: RedisStartupConnectivityTest fails fast only if the JVM property spring.profiles.active contains prod, but prod sets SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE and runs java -jar; fail-fast/timeout/retry-attempts are unread; RedisValidationService logs 'FALLING BACK TO IN-MEMORY' but no bean switches; ApplicationStartupValidator expects 'inmemory', so in-memory reports DEGRADED.

In-memory mode silently drops upload limits: InMemoryStorageRateLimitService overrides only the 2-arg checkUploadAllowed; SignedUrlService calls the 3-arg overload, whose base sees a null RedisTemplate and returns allowed(999,999).

The health signal is inconsistent: readiness ignores Redis while the compose healthcheck uses overall health that includes it, so the signal neither drains traffic nor expresses 'degraded'; sentinel mode has no replica to promote.

invariants: Postgres stays the authority for account status, role and tokenVersion: a banned, deleted or version-bumped session is never accepted because Redis is down.
Brute-force controls (step-up attempts, cooldown, lockout, one-time tokens) fail closed or use a durable store, never reset or bypassed.
Rate limiting keeps enforcing a bounded local limit with hashed keys while degraded.
Liveness never depends on Redis; infrastructure failure surfaces as 503, not 401, so the FE keeps sessions.
UserCacheService, RateLimiterService, GeoLocationCache and StorageRateLimitService remain the ports so redis and no-redis behave alike; ShedLock stays on JDBC.
good_designs: Wrap each Redis-backed port in a resilient decorator with a shared circuit breaker, as RedisRateLimiterService already does: user cache falls back to UserRepository plus a short local TTL, evictions become best-effort after commit, and geo locks fall back to JDBC.

Give every Redis-only store a durable or in-memory implementation behind an interface (step-up state and oobCodes in Postgres with expiry), so storage.mode picks the primary backend rather than the only one and no-redis wiring is fixed.
Publish a DEGRADED health contributor, map Redis connection/timeout exceptions to 503 with Retry-After, and read active profiles from the Environment for fail-fast.
red_flags: Sessions live in Redis, so users lose them (they are HMAC-signed JWT cookies; requests fail because status lookups hit Redis).
The app falls back to in-memory implementations when Redis dies (beans are fixed at startup; only the rate limiter falls back per call).
Prod fails fast at startup without Redis (fail-fast is unread; the system-property check never matches env-var profiles).
Readiness goes DOWN during the outage (readiness is db,diskSpace,liquibase; overall health goes DOWN).
Uploads fail open during the outage (only when the RedisTemplate bean is null; runtime errors end in upload_failed).

architecture.today: storage.mode, read once at startup (in-memory only in application-no-redis.yml), picks Redis or in-memory adapters for UserCacheService, RateLimiterService, GeoLocationCache and StorageRateLimitService via @ConditionalOnProperty; step-up and email-verification state use StringRedisTemplate with no port.
architecture.fit: It keeps these ports and storage.mode as the primary-backend choice, adds runtime fallback around the Redis adapters, and gives step-up and oobCode state a port too.
architecture.breaks: It has services call RedisTemplate directly, adds another mode flag or profile, or refreshes the context to swap beans.

architecture.today: @RateLimit goes through the @Primary GdprCompliantRateLimiterService (delegate fixed at construction) to RedisRateLimiterService, whose Lua call runs in a Resilience4j CircuitBreaker with per-instance memory windows as fallback; it is the only Redis-backed service with a breaker, and RedisConfiguration's cache manager has no CacheErrorHandler.
architecture.fit: It reuses this breaker-and-fallback shape, with one shared breaker configuration, for the user cache, geo lock and upload quotas, and adds a CacheErrorHandler to the existing cache manager.
architecture.breaks: It adds another resilience library, per-class breakers or a second Redis client, or a degraded path that stops counting.

architecture.pattern: Cookie auth with cached status check
architecture.today: JwtAuthenticationFilter validates the HMAC-signed JWT cookie statelessly, then asks UserCacheService (UserRepository only on a miss); exceptions there give 401 on private endpoints and anonymous access on public ones, and 419 marks a stale tokenVersion.
architecture.fit: It reads UserRepository in the adapter when Redis errors, keeps the status and tokenVersion checks, and answers 503 via writeErrorResponse only if Postgres also fails.
architecture.breaks: It skips status or tokenVersion checks, adds a session store or second auth filter, or leaves Redis errors in the catch that returns 401.

architecture.today: GlobalDefaultExceptionHandler renders TranslatableException subclasses as the localized ErrorResponse (NetworkTranslatableException as 503), and the Angular errorInterceptor refresh-retries 401/419, clears a signed-in session only when refresh-session returns 401, and passes 5xx through.
architecture.fit: It throws NetworkTranslatableException for Redis connection and timeout errors, as RedisRateLimiterService does, so users get a localized 503 and keep their session.
architecture.breaks: It lets raw Redis exceptions become 500s, invents a new error body or status, answers 401, or adds a Redis-specific frontend interceptor.

architecture.pattern: Actuator health groups and startup validators
architecture.today: Readiness is db, diskSpace and liquibase and liveness is ping, so Redis affects only overall health, which UploadSystemHealthIndicator's probe turns DOWN; RedisStartupConnectivityTest fails fast only if the JVM property spring.profiles.active contains prod or test.
architecture.fit: It adds a degraded health contributor outside liveness and readiness and makes the existing startup test read profiles from the Environment.
architecture.breaks: It adds a custom status endpoint or another startup gate, puts Redis into liveness or readiness, or adds a probe that turns health DOWN.

architecture.today: Business crons lock via @SchedulerLock and a JdbcTemplateLockProvider on Postgres, but GeoLocationFacade's weekly GeoIP update locks through GeoLocationCache.tryLock, a Redis SET NX whose errors are not caught.
architecture.fit: It keeps ShedLock on JDBC and moves the GeoIP update to @SchedulerLock or a JDBC fallback.
architecture.breaks: It adds a Redis lock provider, a new lock table or a separate lock service.

architecture.today: Side effects that must not roll back writes run in @TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT) handlers that log failures, yet archiveUser and re-consent evict the user cache inside @Transactional methods.
architecture.fit: It moves evictions onto that after-commit path as best effort, so a Redis error cannot roll back archival or re-consent.
architecture.breaks: It keeps evictions in the transaction or builds an outbox or retry queue only for cache invalidation.
